query: For a high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution and exhibiting a favorable strength–ductility combination, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading? Explain the hypothesized mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the same alloy tested under identical conditions without the intervention, define the applicable exposure and loading regime, identify supporting evidence from prior observations, and specify an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a specific grain boundary engineering treatment preserves toughness in a high-entropy alloy after thermal exposure and subsequent loading.
generation.conditions: Thermal exposure followed by mechanical loading
generation.mechanism: Enhanced grain boundary cohesion and resistance to crack propagation due to the grain boundary engineering treatment
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved toughness compared to the untreated alloy under identical conditions
generation.baseline: Toughness of the untreated alloy after thermal exposure and loading
generation.boundary: Limits of thermal exposure and loading conditions beyond which the intervention may not be effective
generation.uncertainty: Effectiveness of the grain boundary engineering treatment for different high-entropy alloy compositions and processing histories

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the toughness of treated and untreated high-entropy alloy specimens after thermal exposure and mechanical loading
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated specimens do not exhibit significantly improved toughness compared to the untreated specimens, the hypothesis is falsified
